sentence: This project builds a treatment and a way to prevent cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
This project supports a gathering of researchers who study how enzymes work inside cells.
This project studies in animals how the fetal foregut splits into the trachea and esophagus and what goes wrong in birth defects.
This project tries to find drug targets in prostate cancer stem cells that drive castration-resistant prostate cancer and drug resistance.
This project teaches advanced statistical methods used in neuroimaging and genetics.
This project tests whether machine learning that finds patients with cancer, plus lay health workers, improves communication about goals of care.
This project builds a system that images the brain using a synthetic compound eye camera and deep-learning based image reconstruction.
This project supports a cancer center that brings together researchers and health professionals to work on preventing and curing cancer.
This project builds a soft electronic and microfluidic micro-lab that screens drugs in organoids and monitors how cells and tissues respond.
This project studies how visceral leishmaniasis spreads in Eastern Africa, including the behavior of sand flies and the host and parasite factors behind disease progression.
This project finds regions of glioblastoma where the immune response is suppressed and studies the cell mechanisms behind them.
This project uses structural modeling and molecular fingerprinting on single-cell T-cell receptor sequencing data to design T-cell-based immunotherapies for acute myeloid leukemia.
This project studies how a protein called Dishevelled and filamentous cellular structures help cells communicate with each other in sea star oocytes.
This project tries to find inherited genetic causes of contralateral breast cancer in women who had radiation therapy.
This project builds open source software that processes, analyzes and shows rodent brain imaging data, including magnetic resonance imaging and optical microscopy.
This project tests whether gain-of-function mutations in a receptor on mast cells cause adverse drug reactions, using humanized mouse models.
This project studies how wildfire smoke exposure changes DNA methylation and immune signatures in mouse and human samples.
This project builds a statistical method that rebuilds the 3D structure of all RNAs from RNA-RNA spatial interaction data.
This project studies how T cell receptor signaling creates long-lasting immunological memory in a type of T cell.
This project builds an automated way to detect and measure secondary lymphedema in head and neck cancer using spatial algorithms and a smartphone.
